evals.name: two-population-trace-stream
evals.prompt: I traced my bf16 GEMV with event0/event1 over 16 calls. The interval stream is sixteen values of 2 and sixteen values between 283 and 295. The min is 2 and the median is 142. After my change the stream is sixteen 2s and sixteen 127s, median 64. How many cycles per call does my kernel take before and after?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes two populations: an instrumented initializer (the zero kernel for the InOut accumulator) at 2 cycles and the GEMV. Separates them (by order, population j = intervals[j::2], or equivalently here by sorting and cutting into groups of 16) and reports the kernel as about 283-295 (median ~291) before and 127 after. Warns that min and median over the mixed stream are meaningless and that the median landing on a matching ratio is coincidence. Suggests confirming via bytes zeroed or by checking which selected sources have event0 markers.
assertions: Identifies that the stream contains two different kernels' intervals (e.g. a zero/initializer kernel plus the GEMV)
Reports the GEMV as roughly 283-295 cycles before and 127 after
States that the min (2) and the median (142/64) of the whole stream should not be quoted as the kernel's cycles
Describes separating the populations before taking statistics, either by call order (every K-th interval) or by splitting the sorted stream into groups of `calls` (16)

evals.name: bit-exact-claim-needs-raw-diff
evals.prompt: I rewrote my sigmoid's `0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2))` as a single mac against an accumulator preloaded with 0.5. The e2e test passes at rtol 0.04. Can I say in the commit message that the change is bit-exact?
evals.expected_output: Says a tolerance pass is not evidence of bit-exactness; rtol 0.04 can hide real changes. Explains why the rewrite should be exact (scaling by a power of two is exact and rounding commutes with it), but requires proof: build both arms in trees differing only in this file, run both on hardware (test_kernels_bench --baseline-sources reports differing_words per case), diff the raw output words, and mutation-prove the diff catches a deliberate small change.
assertions: States that passing a tolerance-based test does not prove the output is bit-identical
Recommends running both old and new builds on hardware and comparing raw output words exactly
Recommends mutation-proving the comparison (a deliberately altered kernel must show a difference)
Gives the reason the rewrite can be exact (multiplying by a power of two is exact / rounding commutes with power-of-two scaling)

evals.name: dispatch-bound-routing
evals.prompt: I made my conv kernel 15x faster in traced cycles per call on the AIE core, but the end-to-end device time for my 16-call test only improved by 30%. Did something go wrong? Should I keep optimizing the kernel?
evals.expected_output: Explains that at this shape dispatch and host overhead (tens of microseconds per run) dominate device time, so wall clock can't reflect the core speedup; computes or explains core_fraction (cycles x calls / clock / device time). The kernel win is real when judged on traced cycles. Further kernel work won't move wall time if the production shape is also dispatch-bound; route to dataflow-level work (aie-dataflow-opt): batching, more work per dispatch, fusion.
assertions: Explains that fixed dispatch/host overhead dominates the measured device time at this shape
Says the traced-cycle speedup is the correct measure of the kernel change
Suggests estimating the core's share of device time (cycles x calls / clock vs device time)
Points to dataflow-level changes (e.g. aie-dataflow-opt, batching, larger or fused work per dispatch) rather than more kernel tuning if the production shape is also dispatch-bound

evals.name: static-report-to-ab
evals.prompt: Here is a static candidate report for leaky_relu: class strong, UNROLL(4), loop byte_count 176 -> 184, II4 -> II5 per 4x the elements, predicted ~90 cycles per call vs 298 now, new remainder case leaky_relu_160. Markers: yes. I have an NPU. Take it from here.
evals.expected_output: Runs the gate first (test_kernels_e2e -m extensive for the case and the new remainder case) and mutation-proves it. Builds a base arm and runs both arms back to back in one test_kernels_bench run with --baseline-sources, a pinned taskset, under the shared NPU lock if one exists. Reads traced cycles per call from the baseline table and the cycles row, checks n against calls, checks an unchanged kernel's case reproduces, compares with the ~90 prediction. Commits one change with base -> after cycles per case and n, and adds an S row to the static table.
assertions: Runs the correctness gate (test_kernels_e2e or equivalent), including the remainder case, before trusting any timing
Measures a base arm and the candidate arm back to back in one session
Measures both arms in one run (test_kernels_bench --baseline-sources) or otherwise keeps the arms' builds apart (separate or wiped NPU_CACHE_HOME)
Compares the measured cycles with the static prediction
Records the outcome (commit with base -> after per case, and/or a new row in the static signal -> HW table)

evals.name: raw-kernel-static-first
evals.prompt: Here's my int8 conv kernel in aie_kernels/aie2p/conv2dk1_i8.cc. It's slow on the NPU. Make it faster.
evals.expected_output: Starts with the static screen per aie-kernel-opt-static (resolve the called symbol, contracts, remarks, libcalls/spills/stack, diagnosis -> candidate with a class) rather than editing and timing blindly, then measures the candidate on hardware with a base arm, back to back.
assertions: Runs or requests the static screen (aie-kernel-opt-static: remarks report, symbol resolution, object checks) before any hardware A/B
Resolves which extern "C" symbol the factory actually calls before editing
Plans a base-vs-candidate hardware measurement rather than a single after-only run

evals.name: shared-tree-provenance
evals.prompt: Three agents are optimizing kernels in one checkout on one NPU. My matmul row improved 33% but I only edited mha.cc. Another agent says their zero.cc fix is uncommitted in the tree. Can I claim the matmul win?
evals.expected_output: No. A row that moved while its file didn't change belongs to something it includes; matmul (and mha) include zero.cc, and the only instrumented population may be zero. Check git diff and git status over the include closure, check which entry symbol the markers bracket (the contract's trace= and the marker audit), split populations by order, and rebuild the base arm by copying the live tree and restoring only one's own files. Record provenance (commit, status over the include closure, arm source dir) next to each number. Serialize NPU access with one shared lock.
assertions: Does not credit the 33% to the user's change
Points to the include closure (zero.cc included by matmul/mha) or the uncommitted teammate edit as the likely source
Recommends checking git status/diff over the include closure and recording provenance per number
Mentions checking which kernel the trace markers bracket, or splitting interval populations
